notes:
Summary: Ironworks (platform for in-IDE developer productivity used by a large internal dev org). Primary interest: low-latency in-IDE copilots (streaming token-level), model/version pinning for predictable developer UX, and cost controls for hundreds of seats. Very cost-sensitive at scale — wants clear unit economics per-seat and per-commit usage.

Key quoted needs / call snippets:
- "If token cost per-seat is variable we're going to blow past budget; need predictable per-seat SKU + burst pricing" — Head of Dev Productivity.
- "Streaming must feel instant in VSCode, target ~50-150ms per token for interactive completions" — Platform eng lead.

Technical requirements / preferences:
- Prefer Dedicated or Private (VPC) for consistent latency and repo/data isolation.
- Strong interest in Redwood Optimize recommendations: quantization profiles that preserve code correctness, and caching strategies for repo-aware prefix caching.
- Want model pinning per team (stable model for CI vs experimental for new hires).
- Expectation for automatic KV/prefix caching across similar repositories and shared company snippets to reduce token counts.
- Need observability: token-level costs by team, per-route latency percentiles, and per-developer monthly spend dashboards.

POC goals and acceptance criteria:
- Baseline: current self-hosted Llama-based cluster yields ~80ms median token latency under internal micro-batching; Redwood should match or beat latency with dedicated pool.
- Cost goal: reduce per-seat monthly inference spend by >=25% vs current self-hosted baseline using caching + quantization without degrading top-1 completion accuracy by >1.5% on our code-eval suite.
- Reliability: fallback policies to lower-cost models when burst capacity reached; failover to hosted region with <1% error rate increase.

Timeline / recent activities (bulleted notes):
- 2025-09-15: Lead created in CRM from inbound trial request.
- 2025-10-02: Discovery call (Maya Chen) — high-level requirements captured.
- 2025-12-11: Security questionnaire sent; asked for SOC2 + KMS integration details.
- 2026-01-20: Technical deep-dive with SE (Diego) — discussed streaming hooks, KV cache ideas.
- 2026-02-12: Intro demo (Fireflies: ff-2026-02-12-ironworks-intro).
- 2026-03-02: POC kickoff; access request for VPC peering, sample repo set, and perf harness (Fireflies: ff-2026-03-02-poc-kickoff).
- 2026-03-08: First POC benchmark run: Redwood Dedicated w/ default quantization: median token latency 78ms, 18% cost reduction vs baseline. Notes: some regressions in completion accuracy for python docstring generation.

Open technical questions / notes for SE team:
- Need a quantization profile that is conservative on code generation tokens; propose mixed-precision profile (int8 for transformer weights, fp16 for output head) — can Redwood provide guidance / repo-specific profiles?
- Cache TTLs: proposed repo-scoped prefix cache with immediate invalidation on push to default branch; legal asks about logs retention.
- Per-seat billing model: customer wants a hybrid (base per-seat + pooled token bucket) to cap predictable spend but allow bursts.

Next actions (short bullet-style):
- SE to produce quantization-sensitivity report (due 2026-03-18).
- Deliver updated pricing sheet with hybrid per-seat model (Maya).
- Legal to review and redline residency appendix (customer legal team requested 10 business days).
- Run expanded POC tests on quantized model variants against Ironworks' code-eval suite (2 more runs).
